## Impact

An authenticated user who can publish to a channel on a server running in
cluster mode can make the server allocate a heap buffer far smaller than
the message it is about to copy into it, and then write past the end of
that buffer with attacker-controlled bytes. This reliably crashes the
server process, and because the overflowing bytes are chosen by the
attacker, it may be possible to escalate it to remote code execution
running as the user the server runs as.

This issue affects Valkey 7.2, 8.0, 8.1, 9.0, 9.1 and 9.2 running in
cluster mode. Servers that do not have cluster mode enabled are not
affected.

## Details

When a node propagates a `PUBLISH` or `SPUBLISH` to the rest of the
cluster, `clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock` in `src/cluster_legacy.c`
(`src/cluster.c` on 7.2) computes the length of the cluster bus message as
a `size_t`, but passes it to `createClusterMsgSendBlock`, which takes a
`uint32_t`. When the channel and message together exceed `UINT32_MAX`, the
length is silently truncated and a buffer far smaller than the message is
allocated. The two `memcpy` calls that follow copy the full channel and
message into it. Both the regular and the light cluster bus header paths
are affected, as are the module publish APIs.

Building a channel and message this large requires more than 4 GiB of
memory. With the default `proto-max-bulk-len` of 512 MB, a client cannot
send arguments that large directly, but a script can construct them on the
server.

The cluster bus cannot represent a message of this size, so the fix
validates the complete serialized length before any 32-bit conversion or
allocation. `PUBLISH` and `SPUBLISH` now reply with an error, and the
message is neither published locally nor propagated.

## Mitigation

You can mitigate this issue by using Valkey ACLs to restrict the scripting
commands (`EVAL`, `EVALSHA`, `EVAL_RO`, `EVALSHA_RO`, `FCALL`, `FCALL_RO`
and `FUNCTION`) if your application does not intend to use them, and by
not raising `proto-max-bulk-len` above its default.

## Credits

The defect was reported by Nenad Stojanovski working with Trend Micro Zero
Day Initiative (ZDI-CAN-28318). The fix was authored by
https://github.com/roshkhatri (#5030).
